texts.preamble: Pushpangadhan T.D vs The Food Inspector on 14 January, 2016 Author: B.Sudheendra Kumar Bench: B.Sudheendra Kumar In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice B.Sudheendra Kumar Thursday, The 14Th Day Of January 2016/24Th Pousha, 1937 Crl.Rev.Pet.No. 1247 of 2009 ( ) --------------------------------- Crl.A 11/2004 Of The Additional Sessions Court (Adhoc-Iii), North Paravur St 6731/1998 Of The Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, North Paravur Revision Petitioner/Appellant/Accused: -------------------------------------- Pushpangadhan T.D., S/O.Dasan T.R., Aged 40 Years, Tharayil Parambu, Muttinakam Po Varapuzha, Ernakulam District. By Advs.Sri.Santhosh Subramanian Sri.E.A.Thankappan Sri.Sherry J. Thomas Sri.S.Sreekumar(North Paravur) Respondent(S)/Respondents/Complainant: ------------------------------------- 1. The Food Inspector, Edappally Circle, Ernakulam District. 2. The State Of Kerala, Rep.By Public Prosecutor, High Court Of Kerala.
texts.facts: The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 1.8.1998, PW2, the Food Inspector purchased 750 ml. of cow milk from the shop of the first accused. The second accused was the owner of the said shop. After sampling as per rules, one sample was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis. The Public Analyst, after analysis submitted Ext.P3 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for cow milk under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules and was therefore adulterated. It was further opined in Ext.P3 report that the sample contained not less than 7% of added water as calculated from the milk solids not fat content under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW5 were examined and Exts.P1 to P17 were marked for the prosecution. No evidence was adduced on the side of the revision petitioner.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext.P3 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. 6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act. Therefore, Ext. P3 report of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that Pushpangadhan T.D vs The Food Inspector on 14 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127036394/ 2 the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra). It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal. In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused. The matter was referred to a Division Bench and the Division Bench also affirmed the said decision, submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
